report.verdict: Customer Success and a book of 85 mid-market accounts caught my attention. The renewal and onboarding work backs that up, and I’d write to you. I’d still ask what kinds of issues you handled in support.
write_up: Customer success at a shipping software company is the story here, with support experience before it. It’s common to use the headline and About to announce a search, but yours leave the account and renewal work further down.

The Parcelwise account work is the model. You name the book of 85 mid-market accounts, the quarterly business reviews and the 91% renewed by revenue in 2025. That gives a stranger a clear picture of your work.

Start by bringing that work into the headline and opening of your About. Then put a standard customer success title beside Customer Happiness Hero II and add the kinds of tickets you handled as a Support Specialist. Someone hiring for customer success can then connect your account work and support background without guessing.

cards.line: Open to work | Seeking new opportunities in Customer Success
cards.cannot_tell: The search takes up the headline, while your mid-market account work sits further down. Put customer success and your specialty first.
cards.example: Customer Success | mid-market accounts | shipping software
cards.question: What were the main customer goals you worked on across those accounts?

cards.line: Customer success professional currently seeking my next opportunity. Open to remote roles. Please reach out if you think I could be a fit for your team.
cards.cannot_tell: This tells a recruiter what you’re looking for, but not what you do. Your account book and renewal work give you a stronger opening.
cards.example: I managed a book of 85 mid-market accounts for a shipping software company. I ran quarterly business reviews and renewal conversations, and renewed 91% of accounts by revenue in 2025. I wrote the onboarding guide new accounts get in their first week.
cards.question: What kind of customer success work are you looking to do next?

cards.where: Parcelwise, Customer Happiness Hero II title
cards.cannot_tell: This title means something at Parcelwise, but it doesn’t name the account work you describe below it. A standard title beside it would give that work a name a recruiter can search for.
cards.example: Customer Happiness Hero II ([standard customer success job title])
cards.question: At another company, would this job be called Customer Success Manager or Account Manager?

cards.where: Parcelwise, Customer Happiness Hero II description
cards.line: Ran quarterly business reviews and renewal conversations; renewed 91% of accounts by revenue in 2025.
cards.cannot_tell: This is the line to copy. You name the work and the renewal figure, so a recruiter doesn’t have to guess what happened.
Tickets in Zendesk are a start, but the types of customer issues you handled aren’t here. The line has no words for troubleshooting or ticket triage, if you did either.
cards.example: Answered support tickets in Zendesk about [types of customer issues], [how often].
cards.question: What kinds of customer issues did you handle in Zendesk, and how often?

cards.cannot_tell: Problem Solving could describe almost any job. Your quarterly business reviews and renewal conversations say more about the customer success work you’ve done.
cards.example: Zendesk | quarterly business reviews | renewal conversations
cards.question: Which renewal tasks did you handle most often at Parcelwise?

fit.why: Your headline names Customer Success, and your latest Parcelwise job describes account management, renewals and onboarding.
fit.level: mid-level, Customer Happiness Hero II and a book of 85 mid-market accounts
fit.note: ‘Customer Success’ is in your headline and About. ‘mid-market accounts’ and ‘quarterly business reviews’ are in your latest Parcelwise description. ‘Zendesk’ is in your top skills and Support Specialist description. ‘Customer Success Manager’, ‘account management’ and ‘customer retention’ aren’t on your profile. Add the standard title to your headline and the other terms to your latest job description only if they describe your work. Start by moving the customer success title into your headline.
